title: Tracking neuronal motility in live murine retinal explants
protocol: Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation.
Enucleate eyes and transfer to ice-cold RPMI 1640 medium using forceps.

Isolate neural retina by dissection under a dissection microscope in ice-cold RPMI 1640 medium by removing all non-neural tissues (cornea, sclera, iris, choroid, lens, optic nerve, retinal pigment epithelium, and ciliary body) using forceps.
Remove all pigmented non-neural retinal tissues.
Transfer retina from explant culture to ice-cold RPMI 1640 medium.
Isolate neural retina by dissection under a dissection microscope in ice-cold RPMI 1640 medium.
Remove lens with forceps.
Apply four equidistant radial cuts using fine scissors going halfway towards the centre of the retina.
Transfer retina in a small drop of RPMI 1640 medium onto the edge portion of a microscopy glass slide using a sterile plastic Pasteur pipette with manually widened opening.
Place photoreceptors facing the glass slide and retinal ganglion cells facing the user.
Carefully flatten retina onto glass slide by unfolding petals using fine forceps.
Remove some RPMI 1640 to aid flattening.
Care must be taken to not introduce tissue damage during flattening and unfolding petals.
Remove most of RPMI 1640 medium using lint-free tissue paper.
Place a 0.45 μm MF-Millipore™ nitrocellulose membrane on the retina with ganglion cell layer touching the membrane.
Transfer membrane-mounted retina back into RPMI 1640 medium by dipping the edge of the glass slide into medium.
Fix membrane with retina facing up to the bottom of a Ø5.5 cm tissue culture petri dish on a thin layer of vacuum grease.
Press down membrane onto vacuum grease using blunt tools.
Place a platinum ring over the membrane.
Fill the dish with 10 mL DMEMgfp-2 live imaging medium.
Transfer imaging dish containing flat-mounted retina to microscope environmental chamber pre-equilibrated to 37°C/5% CO2.
Allow tissue to acclimatize to 37°C/5% CO2 for at least 30 minutes prior to initiating time-lapse recording.
Introduce a water-immersion objective pre-sterilized with 70% ethanol into the live imaging medium.
Affix CO2 supplying apparatus to the live imaging dish.
Identify suitable field of view by scanning through microscope eyepiece.
Tune the multiphoton laser source to a wavelength suitable for 2-photon excitation of the fluorescent protein(s) of interest.
Ensure that the laser and detector(s) have been properly set up for signal detection.
Apply a layer of paraffin oil, pre-equilibrated to 37°C, on top of the live imaging medium.
Prevent medium evaporation during time-lapse recording by applying the paraffin oil layer.
Initiate time-lapse recording.
Acquire xyzt image series at a resolution of 512 × 512 pixels.
Use a step size of 1 μm for acquiring images.
Record images at 10 min intervals.
Ensure that imaging duration frequently reaches up to 12 h, based on tissue health and integrity.
Monitor the field of view for any pigmented cells that absorb infrared light.
Adjust focus if necessary due to tissue drift.
Process xyzt image series in Fiji/ImageJ with standard imaging processing tools for noise reduction.
Register xyzt image series using the ‘Correct 3D drift’ plug-in for automated drift correction based on automated landmark recognition.
Register xyzt image series manually using the ‘Descriptor-based series registration (2D/3D + t)’ plug-in if automated registration failed and landmarks had to be defined manually.
Export registered xyzt image series as *.tif file.
Perform cell tracking using software of choice.
Identify rod cell bodies based on size and location parameters within the software.
Manually validate generated trajectories to avoid data artifacts in subsequent analysis steps.
Export completed cell tracking data as a *.xls file.
Open and run the Matlab script 'MSDforztrackingdata.m'.
Navigate to the source trajectory file when prompted by the script.
Calculate AvMSD using the equation M S D ( Δ t ) =   1  N − n    ∑  i = 1   N − n     [  z  (   (  i + n  )  δ t  )  − z  ( i δ t )   ]  2.
Specify the range of trajectory IDs to be analyzed from the source file, for example: group = [1, 2, 3].
Open and run 'ztrajectory_gen.m' to convert read-in trajectory data stored in array format into matrix 'ztrajectories'.
Calculate lengths of individual trajectories by iterating through each trajectory.
Initialize a vector 'lengths' with ones for each trajectory length.
For each trajectory, determine the actual length and store it in 'lengths'.
Determine maximum trajectory length as 't'.
Create a zero-filled matrix 'ztrajectories' to hold all converted trajectories.
Iterate over each trajectory, adding leading NaN values if necessary.
Concatenate actual z-axis positions with any trailing NaN values for incomplete paths.
Open and run 'Trajectory_analysis.m'.
Generate result outputs in matrix format denoted ‘dfff2’ for smoothened instantaneous velocity values.
Generate result outputs in matrix format denoted ‘d2fff2’ for smoothened instantaneous acceleration values.
Obtain un-smoothened instantaneous velocity data stored in ‘dyyy’.
Plot and interpret data generated in software of choice, e.g., Matlab or Graphpad Prism.
Plot AvMSD (± standard errors) vs time lag (e.g., 0, 10, 20, 30,…n min).
Apply linear function curve fitting to obtain the slope ‘2D’ and subsequently calculate ‘D’ to quantitatively compare AvMSD steepness for random/non-directional motion.
Apply quadratic function curve fitting y = a x^2 to obtain the quadratic factor ‘a’ as numerical representation of curve steepness for directed motions.
Plot instantaneous velocity and acceleration values as histograms to show frequency distributions.
